requirements.title: Branching transfers control to a labeled branch target in the same inclusive scope
requirements.definition: Branching is the Fortran control-transfer concept that alters the normal execution sequence by transferring control from one statement to a labeled branch target statement in the same inclusive scope. GO TO, computed GO TO, alternate-return CALL, and I/O END=, EOR=, or ERR= specifiers can cause branches. Procedure references and control constructs can transfer control but are not branches. The paragraph also enumerates the statement kinds that can serve as branch targets.
